hero.h1: Usability testing services that catch problems before production
hero.sub: Real users, real tasks, real feedback. We test concepts, prototypes, and live products before development and before launch.

summary: Moderated studies, concept validation, and A/B testing that catch problems before they ship.
sourceContext: US UI/UX design agency; this page sells task-based usability testing rounds to teams validating prototypes and live products before launch.
abstract: Usability testing services measure how real users complete tasks on a prototype or live product through moderated sessions, unmoderated studies and System Usability Scale (SUS) scoring, before a user experience (UX) team ships the design. Our usability testing engagement takes 4–8 weeks, costs $25,000–$60,000, and runs 2–3 test rounds with design fixes between rounds.

sections.answer: Usability testing is a research method in which representative users attempt realistic tasks on a product while a researcher observes where the users succeed, hesitate and fail. Each usability test measures task success rate, time on task and errors, the effectiveness and efficiency measures of ISO 9241-11.
sections.body: Usability testing differs from UX audit services in one way: recruited users evaluate the product, not designers. Nielsen Norman Group guidance sets 5 users per round for a qualitative usability test, so a UX team runs several small rounds instead of 1 large round.

sections.h2: What do usability testing services include?
sections.answer: Our usability testing services include 6 deliverables: a test plan, participant recruitment, moderated usability sessions, unmoderated usability studies, SUS and Single Ease Question scoring, and a usability test report.

items.title: Test plan.
items.body: Tasks, success criteria and participant profiles are written for each round, for example "find and book a 30-minute appointment".

items.title: Participant recruitment.
items.body: 5–8 participants per round are screened to match real user groups, for example first-time buyers and repeat buyers.

items.title: Moderated usability sessions.
items.body: A researcher runs 45–60-minute think-aloud sessions over Lookback or Zoom, for example on a clickable Figma prototype.

items.title: Unmoderated usability studies.
items.body: Maze or UserTesting runs task-based studies with 20–50 participants, for example a first-click test on a new navigation.

items.title: SUS and Single Ease Question scoring.
items.body: Every participant answers the 10-item System Usability Scale and the 7-point Single Ease Question (SEQ), for example a SUS score out of 100 per round.

items.title: Usability test report.
items.body: Every finding gets a video clip, a severity rating from 1 to 4 and a recommended design fix.

sections.h2: How does the usability testing process work?
sections.answer: The usability testing process takes 4–8 weeks (20–40 working days) and runs in 6 steps, from the test plan to the final report.

items.title: Test planning (2–4 days)
items.body: We agree the tasks, user groups, success criteria and the prototype or live build to test.

items.title: Participant recruitment (5–8 days)
items.body: We screen and schedule 5–8 participants per user group for the first round.

items.title: Round 1 sessions (3–5 days)
items.body: Moderated and unmoderated sessions run on the prototype, and every session is recorded.

items.title: Analysis and design fixes (5–12 days)
items.body: Findings are rated by severity, and designers fix the highest-severity issues in Figma.

items.title: Round 2 sessions (3–6 days)
items.body: A second round with new participants tests the fixed design against the round 1 task success rate.

items.title: Report and handover (2–5 days)
items.body: We present the usability test report and video highlights in a 60-minute session.

sections.h2: What are the benefits of usability testing?
sections.answer: Usability testing has 4 benefits: usability testing increases task success rate, improves design quality before launch, reduces post-launch rework and develops a usability benchmark.

items.title: Increases task success rate
items.body: Fixing observed failures between rounds increases the share of participants who complete each task without help.

items.title: Improves design quality before launch
items.body: Testing prototypes improves interaction patterns, labels and error messages before any code ships.

items.title: Reduces post-launch rework
items.body: Catching usability issues in a Figma prototype reduces the development days spent fixing live code.

items.title: Develops a usability benchmark
items.body: SUS scores from each round develop a benchmark that shows usability change release after release.

sections.answer: Usability testing explains why users fail a task through observed sessions; A/B testing measures which of 2 live versions converts better through a traffic split. Teams run usability testing first to find the fix, then A/B testing to measure the fix at scale.

sections.h2: How much does usability testing cost?
sections.answer: Usability testing costs $25,000–$60,000 and takes 4–8 weeks. The price depends on 4 factors: the number of test rounds, the number of participants per round, the number of platforms and the recruitment difficulty.
sections.body: An engagement of 2 moderated rounds with 5 participants each on 1 web prototype sits near $25,000. An engagement of 3 rounds on web and mobile, with 8 participants per round, unmoderated Maze studies and hard-to-recruit participants, for example physicians, sits near $60,000. Teams that need broader discovery before testing start with UX research services.

sections.h2: When should a product team run usability testing?
sections.answer: A product team should run usability testing in 5 situations:
items: A redesign is ready for development, if no real user has tried the new flows.
Conversion rate drops after a release, if analytics cannot show why users stop.
A new product enters beta, if the team needs evidence before launch.
2 design concepts compete, if stakeholders cannot agree on 1 direction.
A healthcare or finance product launches, if regulators or buyers expect documented usability evidence.

sections.answer: These answers cover the 5 questions buyers ask most about usability testing services.

faqs.q: How many users are needed for usability testing?
faqs.a: Usability testing needs 5 users per round for a qualitative test and 40 users for a quantitative test, per Nielsen Norman Group guidance.

faqs.q: What is the difference between moderated and unmoderated usability testing?
faqs.a: Moderated usability testing has a researcher present to ask follow-up questions, while unmoderated usability testing runs on tools such as Maze without a researcher and reaches more participants in less time.

faqs.q: Can usability testing be done on a prototype?
faqs.a: Yes. Usability testing on a clickable Figma prototype finds usability issues before development starts.

faqs.q: Does usability testing include A/B testing?
faqs.a: Yes. Our usability testing services include A/B testing plans and analysis for live products with enough traffic to reach statistical significance.

faqs.q: How long does usability testing take?
faqs.a: Usability testing takes 4–8 weeks, which equals 20–40 working days, for 2–3 test rounds; a single usability testing round takes 1–3 weeks.
